blocks.text: Gimel Hebrew Letter (ג): Sound, Words & Practice

Gimel (ג) is the third letter of the Hebrew alphabet. It is pronounced with a hard [g] sound, similar to the [g] in the English word "good." In modern Hebrew, Gimel is generally pronounced consistently, though slight variations may occur depending on the speaker's accent or dialect.

The Hebrew word 'גַג' [gag], meaning 'roof,' consists of two Gimel (ג) letters. A patach (ַ) appears under the first Gimel, giving it the [a] sound, similar to the [a] in "father." The second Gimel follows without a vowel, maintaining the [g] sound.

The Hebrew word 'אַגַב' [agav], meaning 'by the way' or 'incidentally,' consists of three letters: Aleph (א), Gimel (ג), and Bet (ב). A patach (ַ) appears under both Aleph and Gimel, giving them the [a] sound. The final Bet (ב) is pronounced as [v] since it lacks a dagesh.

You've now learned Gimel (ג), the third letter of the Hebrew alphabet. In this lesson, we explored two new words that feature Gimel and reinforced our understanding of previous letters, Aleph (א) and Bet (ב), along with the patach vowel. Keep practicing and listening to the audio examples to solidify your knowledge!
